independent_reconstruction.alternative_route: One may first extend the frame by an orthonormal-basis theorem. That is a dependency furnishing the assumed seed, not an additional requested construction-cost claim.
independent_reconstruction.conclusion: If r<N there is an orientation-corrected orthogonal W with det W=1 and W[:,e(a)]=V[:,a] for every a. The positive statement must be joined to an explicit failure of the universal extension when r=N.

derivation.argument: Take determinants in U^T U=I. Since det(U^T)=det U and det I=1, (det U)^2=1. Over R, (det U-1)(det U+1)=0, giving the two cases. No target orientation is assumed.
If every ambient column were in the range, e would be surjective and finite cardinality would imply N<=r. This contradicts r<N. The actual physical column indices need not form a prefix.
Define S_j[k,k]=-1 for k=j and 1 otherwise, with zero off-diagonal entries. Each squared diagonal entry is 1, so S_j^T S_j=I. The determinant is the product of the diagonal entries, exactly -1.
derivation.claim: A diagonal sign flip at j is orthogonal with determinant -1.

derivation.argument: If det U=1 take W=U. Otherwise take W=U S_j. Then W^T W=S_j^T(U^T U)S_j=I, det W=(-1)(-1)=1, and (U S_j)[i,e(a)]=U[i,e(a)] because e(a)!=j. Multiplication on the right is load-bearing: it rescales columns, not rows.
derivation.claim: Right multiplication repairs the negative determinant without changing prescribed columns.

derivation.argument: Set N=r=2, e=id and V=diag(1,-1). V^T V=I and det V=-1. Any W preserving every prescribed column satisfies W=V entrywise, so det W=-1 and cannot equal +1. All positions are fixed, hence the unused-column construction has no available position.
derivation.claim: The r=N universal extension is false.

derivation.argument: At r=N a fully prescribed orientation-positive frame already belongs to SO(N), so a completion may exist. The counterexample defeats an unconditional theorem after dropping r<N; it does not assert impossibility for all full frames. The empty N=r=0 matrix has determinant 1 and is another valid full-frame boundary. The positive r<N branch excludes N=0 automatically.
derivation.claim: Strict inequality is sufficient for every orthonormal prescribed frame, not necessary for each successful instance.

independent_reconstruction.objects: N,r are natural numbers; V is a real N by r matrix with V^T V=I_r; e:Fin r -> Fin N is injective and assigns the prescribed columns. question_input.question: Suppose r orthonormal real columns are placed at r distinct positions among the N columns of an orthogonal matrix, and suppose r < N so at least one column position is left free. The naive completion to an orthogonal matrix may land in the reflection family (determinant -1) rather than the rotation family (determinant +1). Prove that one can always repair the orientation so the final matrix has determinant exactly +1 while leaving every one of the r prescribed columns completely unchanged. Explain why the strict inequality r < N is exactly what makes the repair possible, and why the repair cannot in general be done when r = N.

independent_reconstruction.alternative_route: Either telescope explicit P U P^{-1} products or prove multiplicativity of the induced reindex algebra equivalence and induct on the gate list. The latter still needs an explicit bridge explaining P and both boundary maps.
independent_reconstruction.conclusion: The consistently renamed primitive circuit evaluates to P (U_t ... U_1) P^{-1}, with exact finite witnesses refuting one-sided multiplication and the unrelated-basis-permutation reading. Empty-circuit, zero/one-wire and physical-routing boundaries are part of the question.

derivation.argument: R_sigma(b)(sigma(w))=b(w). Its inverse is R_(sigma^{-1}), since composing the wire maps cancels. Thus P is a permutation matrix and P^{-1}=P^T=P^dagger.
derivation.claim: The induced bitstring action is a bijection and transports each original wire value to its renamed location.

derivation.argument: On basis input b, X at target t changes only b(t); after R_sigma this is the bit at sigma(t). CX reads the original control c and flips the distinct target t conditionally; renaming both locations reads the same bit b(c) and changes sigma(t), retaining the distinctness premise. RY/RZ apply the same 2 by 2 coefficients and angle to target values while requiring equal spectator bitstrings. Renaming is bijective on spectator locations, so the amplitudes and context-equality test agree. Linearity then yields U_prime P=P U and hence U_prime=P U P^{-1}.
derivation.claim: Each renamed primitive satisfies U_prime P=P U.

derivation.argument: If output and input labels are a,b, the conjugated matrix entry is U[R_sigma^{-1}(a),R_sigma^{-1}(b)]=U[a composed with sigma,b composed with sigma]. The chronological renamed product is (P U_t P^{-1})...(P U_1 P^{-1}); associativity and each interior P^{-1}P=I give P(U_t...U_1)P^{-1}. Reversing chronological order would be a different operation.
derivation.claim: Two-sided matrix entries and chronological multiplication agree.

derivation.argument: For no gates the empty product is I and P I P^{-1}=I. Fin 0 has the unique empty permutation and Fin 1 has only the identity, so both induce P=I. The N=0 basis space still has one empty bitstring and its identity matrix is 1 by 1; it is not a zero-dimensional state space. Therefore no nontrivial wire-swap counterexample exists at N=0 or 1.
derivation.claim: Empty and small-wire cases have the stated boundaries.

derivation.argument: For N>=2 swap wires 0 and 1, fixing all others. Its bitstring permutation P exchanges the state with bit 1 at wire 0 only and the state with bit 1 at wire 1 only, so P!=I; it also has P^2=I. Output-only F(M)=P M maps two separate identity stages to F(I)F(I)=P^2=I, whereas F(II)=P. Thus the one-sided map does not preserve products. N=2 suffices as an explicit witness; the same transposition embeds into larger N.
derivation.claim: Output-only renaming fails multiplicativity using an actual wire permutation.

derivation.argument: On one wire sigma must be identity, hence a renamed RY(theta) equals RY(theta). Let the unrelated basis swap be X=[[0,1],[1,0]]. With RY(theta)=[[c,-s],[s,c]], c=cos(theta/2), s=sin(theta/2), direct multiplication gives X RY(theta) X=[[c,s],[-s,c]]=RY(-theta). At theta=pi/2, s=sin(pi/4)=sqrt(2)/2>0, so the off-diagonal entries differ. This is exact operator inequality; it need not change all computational measurement probabilities.
derivation.claim: An unrelated basis permutation is not wire renaming, even on one wire.

derivation.argument: An arbitrary permutation matrix P still gives a valid algebra automorphism M -> P M P^{-1}. What fails is identifying that map with changing gate wire labels by sigma when P is unrelated. Nonzero theta alone is not sufficient for unequal rotations: theta=2pi gives sin(theta/2)=0 and both rotations equal -I. Choosing pi/2 makes the witness unequivocal.
derivation.claim: The failure witness has the right quantifiers and preserves the valid algebraic statement.

derivation.argument: The proof changes both basis boundaries and wire names. It inserts no implemented SWAP gates and specifies no hardware connectivity. A fixed physical connectivity graph can attach different routing costs to different wire placements. Algebraic equivalence therefore cannot alone certify equal or zero routing cost.
derivation.claim: Representational equivalence does not establish physical routing cost.

independent_reconstruction.objects: sigma:Fin N equiv Fin N relabels physical wires. For a computational bitstring b, define R_sigma(b)(w)=b(sigma^{-1}(w)). Define P by P|b>=|R_sigma(b)>. P is induced by this sigma; it is not an arbitrary permutation of all basis states. Gate matrices act on column vectors, and the first listed gate acts first.

pitfalls: Swapping sigma with sigma^{-1} between the forward basis map and entry reindex changes conventions.
Output-only P U does not conjugate and is not unital or multiplicative for nontrivial P.
A 2 by 2 basis swap on one wire is not a physical-wire swap.
A witness that assumes only P!=I without furnishing an actual wire permutation does not satisfy the requested witness.
A scalar or global phase equality does not replace exact operator equality.
Nonzero theta does not guarantee RY(theta)!=RY(-theta); choose a concrete valid angle.
Do not omit counterexamples and small-register cases while labeling eval_circuit as full-question coverage.
Do not promote hardware routing assertions without a hardware model.

question_input.question:
Let sigma be a bijection of the N physical wires, sigma:Fin N equiv Fin N. Its INDUCED bitstring bijection is R_sigma(b)(w)=b(sigma^{-1}(w)); define P by P|b>=|R_sigma(b)>. Thus P is specifically this wire-induced basis permutation, not an arbitrary permutation of all2^N computational labels. A primitive circuit has chronological matrices U_1,...,U_t, with first-listed gate acting first. Consistently rename each gate's target and each control by sigma, retaining gate kind and angle.

Prove that the renamed circuit realizes P(U_t...U_1)P^{-1}, rather than insertion of a one-sided physical permutation. Justify the single-gate conjugation from the induced bitstring action and show the interior inverse/permutation cancellations through the chronological product. Explain why output-only relabeling fails to preserve products, giving two identity stages and an actual nontrivial involutive wire swap as a witness when N>=2. Include empty circuit and N=0,1 boundaries. Finally assess why the same wire-renaming assertion would be false if P were an arbitrary unrelated basis-label permutation: on one wire compare P=X with a nonzero RY. Distinguish algebraic basis reindexing from a physical SWAP/routing implementation; no hardware routing cost follows for free.
